# Data

- DAT-009: Data access with EF Core follows its efficient-querying guidance. It's important not to rush into optimization without data showing a problem. Limit the amount of data going back and forth on the wire: we should only load what's needed. A no-tracking query should be used when the entities retrieved don't need to be updated. Give thought to limiting the number of results, and consider keyset pagination instead of Skip and Take when users move one page at a time. For related data you know in advance you need, eager loading is always better, and it is recommended to avoid lazy loading. Avoid ToList or ToArray before another LINQ operator. Always use asynchronous APIs rather than synchronous ones, and avoid mixing the two in one application. Raw SQL should generally be a last resort.
- DAT-010: Raw SQL is parameterized: FromSql, SqlQuery and ExecuteSql with an interpolated string, which EF Core turns into parameters, should be used wherever possible, and their Raw forms take explicit parameters. Never concatenate or interpolate an untrusted value into the text of a Raw call, and never escape one by hand. Where a part can't be a parameter, such as a column name, map the caller's choice to a strict allow-list of fixed values the app owns, so no Raw call carries a caller's text.
